services.name: The Trocadero Ballroom
services.desc: When John Mulvihill acquired Elitch Gardens in 1916, he agreed to two conditions from the previous owner, Mary Elitch Long: the park’s name would never change, and Mary would be allowed to live out her days on the grounds. With those promises in place, Mulvihill set about modernizing the park, and in 1917 he unveiled its most glamorous addition yet - the Trocadero Ballroom, named for the celebrated dance hall in Paris. The new building stood out even amid Elitch’s already-storied grounds, its yellow stucco walls trimmed in green and white awnings that echoed the nearby carousel. services.name: Venue Rentals
services.desc: The Historic Elitch Theatre seats 650 guests and we have a very large stage and back-stage area. For a production on the stage, or a corporate event in the auditorium, the rental does not include use of the stage by the full audience. For events on the stage or on the patio, such as a reception, an additional rental fee is charged. The lawn in front of the theatre can be rented as well, but this rental includes a rental of the theatre restrooms. (There are no public restrooms in the area.) Since the Carousel is an open public space, rentals are primarily reserved for nonprofit public events, but short private events (under one hour) may be considered. services.name: Haunted History Tours
services.desc: Every theatre has its ghosts-but few carry a history as deep and mysterious as the Historic Elitch Theatre. Built in 1891 and celebrating its 135th anniversary this year, this legendary landmark has welcomed generations of Broadway icons and Hollywood greats to its stage. Now, XXParanormal and the Historic Elitch Theatre invite you to step behind the curtain for an immersive journey through time. Your tour begins with the remarkable story of the theatre and the surrounding grounds, setting the stage for what comes next: a guided exploration into the paranormal personalities believed to linger within these historic walls.
